text:
olivia: Following up from today's all-hands: this thread is for security/privacy/compliance Qs (SOC2/ISO, VPC patterns, KMS/BYOK, audit logs, pen test & bug bounty). Panel: @mari (Security), @raj (CTO), @jeff (Product). Keep Qs short and we'll answer here. :lock:

devon: Sales needs a firm date for SOC2 Type II to tell customers  any chance we can give an exact month?

mari: We're targeting a signed Type II report by Nov 2025. Auditor fieldwork is scheduled for a window in OctNov; exact sign-off depends on auditor queries but Nov is the date Sales can cite. Scope covers Hosted API + Redwood-managed Dedicated.

hana: For Dedicated, do we support AWS PrivateLink or only VPC peering for network connectivity? Customers ask about traffic staying on the AWS backbone.

raj: We support both PrivateLink and VPC peering depending on customer preference and scale. PrivateLink is recommended where you want endpoint isolation and no route table changes; peering is available for high-throughput, low-cost connectivity. For Dedicated we provide an infra checklist: enable required endpoints, update security groups to allow Redwood egress CIDR, and validate DNS resolution for PrivateLink.

devon: KMS question: can a customer use an on-prem HSM (PKCS#11) instead of AWS KMS?

mari: Yes  we support three modes: Redwood-managed KMS, customer-managed cloud KMS (AWS/Azure/GCP BYOK), and HSM-backed keys. For HSM we support CloudHSM and customer HSM via PKCS#11 bridges for the Private/on-prem product. Integration requires a short handshake: key-wrapping policy, a cert-based auth, and an agreed key-rotation schedule.

hana: Can you paste a minimal cross-account KMS grant example we can share?

mari: Minimal example (simplified):

```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Sid": "GrantRedwoodAccess", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDCLOUD:role/RedwoodKMS"}, "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"], "Resource": "*"}
  ]
}
```

jeff: Audit logs  what we ship by default and retention?

mari: Default retention for Hosted is 540 days (we bumped it to support longer investigations), Dedicated includes 365 days with options to extend to multi-year archival, and Private/on-prem retention is controlled by the customer. We support WORM-style immutable exports to cold storage as an add-on and signed, time-stamped exports for dispute resolution.

jeff: Logs include request_id, masked_tenant_id, model, model_version, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, latency_ms, route, decision_reason, and a salted prompt_hash for correlation. We offer configurable pre-export redaction (regex + deterministic hashing) and PII policy templates.

security-bot: Reminder: evidence owners, final upload deadline for SOC2 artifacts is 2025-09-30. Use the evidence portal: https://portal.redwood.com/evidence. :rotating_light:

olivia: Follow-ups well produce this week: (1) one-page "Network Options for Dedicated" (PrivateLink vs Peering), (2) KMS BYOK & HSM checklist, (3) audit-log schema (ndjson sample + field defs). We'll post links when live and loop in Sales for the SOC2 date. If anyone has urgent customer asks, DM the account lead and cc @mari. :thumbsup:
